findings.title: Analytics recording assumes request.user.id is always available
findings.body: The endpoint records analytics with user_id=request.user.id before checking feature flags or request-body validity. This endpoint also supports org auth tokens (it later checks is_org_auth_token_auth(request.auth)), where request.user may be anonymous or not a normal user. If request.user has no usable id, this can fail or record invalid analytics. Since user_id is optional in the analytics event, this should be guarded (e.g., getattr(request.user, 'id', None)).

findings.title: Unbounded report array can cause resource exhaustion on an unauthenticated endpoint
findings.body: The browser reporting collector endpoint is unauthenticated and iterates over every element in the incoming JSON array, validating each one with a DRF serializer. There is no cap on the number of reports or on the size/depth of each report body. A malicious client can POST a very large array or deeply nested bodies, causing CPU, memory, and log pressure. Add a maximum report count and/or body-size limits.

findings.title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validation uses truthiness and misses zero values
findings.body: validate_timestamp checks self.initial_data.get('age') and validate_age checks self.initial_data.get('timestamp') using truthiness. Because 0 is falsy, a report with timestamp present and age=0, or age present and timestamp=0, bypasses the intended mutual-exclusion validation. Additionally, age has no min_value, so negative ages are accepted. This allows invalid browser reports to be accepted and counted.

findings.title: Full unauthenticated request body is logged at INFO level
findings.body: The endpoint logs the entire browser reporting request body at INFO level: logger.info('browser_report_received', extra={'request_body': request.data}). These reports are unauthenticated and can contain URLs, user-agent strings, and other potentially sensitive or user-controlled data. This can create privacy issues and log-volume abuse. Log only metadata or redact/sanitize request bodies.

findings.title: Error events can be mismatched with nodestore data when zipping values
findings.body: fetch_error_details builds node_ids from error_ids, calls nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids), then zips error_ids with events.values(). get_multi returns a mapping, and missing keys or implementation-specific ordering mean events.values() is not guaranteed to align with error_ids. This can associate the wrong title/message/timestamp with an error id or silently drop entries, producing incorrect AI summary input. Look up each event by its generated node id instead of zipping values.

findings.title: Feature-flagged table widget renders hardcoded empty data instead of widget results
findings.body: When organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization') is true, WidgetCardChart renders TableWidgetVisualization with columns={[]} and tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}}. It ignores the actual table result data, meta, fields, aliases, and loading state. Users with this flag enabled will see an empty table instead of the dashboard widget's query results. The visualization needs to be wired to result.data, result.meta, and the derived columns.

findings.title: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES are only hidden while searching
findings.body: The Attributes component returns the sorted attribute list unchanged when searchQuery is empty, and only applies the HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filter inside the search branch. As a result, internal attributes such as is_segment, project_id, and received remain visible in the default unfiltered view. The hidden-attribute filter should be applied before or independent of search filtering.

findings.title: PR comment template inserts unescaped issue title and environment into Markdown
findings.body: MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE formats issue titles and environment names directly into a Markdown link: '* ‼️ [**{title}**]({url}){environment}'. Issue titles and environment names can contain Markdown metacharacters such as brackets or backticks, which can break the link formatting or produce unintended Markdown in GitHub/GitLab PR comments. Escape or sanitize these values before templating.

findings.title: PR comment generation may call get_recommended_event for each top issue
findings.body: get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() while building the merged-PR comment body. This is invoked for each issue in the comment, potentially causing expensive event lookups inside a task that formats PR comments. The broad exception handling also hides failures while still adding latency. Consider caching, limiting this lookup, or making environment enrichment asynchronous/optional.
